title: Analytical method for determining the sulfur content of EP (extreme pressure) additives in lubricating oils

The average absorbance value was used for calculations.

steps.title: Weigh and dissolve samples
steps.instruction: Weigh each sulfurized oil sample and dissolve it in butoxyethanol to obtain a final concentration of 1 g L⁻¹. Mix by magnetic stirring for approximately 5 min to ensure complete dissolution, then allow the solution to equilibrate at room temperature (25 ± 2 °C) for at least 5 min before measurement.

steps.title: Prepare calibration solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare calibration solutions using sulfurized FAME samples with known sulfur content covering the range 15–23 wt % and dissolve them in butoxyethanol to the same 1 g L⁻¹ concentration as the samples.

steps.title: Switch on spectrometer
steps.instruction: Turn on the spectrometer and its light source and allow the instrument to stabilize for 20–30 min before any measurements are taken.

steps.title: Measure blank spectrum
steps.instruction: Fill a quartz cuvette with pure butoxyethanol, record a blank spectrum, and use this spectrum for baseline correction of all sample measurements.

steps.title: Condition cuvette
steps.instruction: Rinse the cuvette with the sample solution prior to each measurement, then fill it carefully with the sample solution, avoiding the introduction of air bubbles.

steps.title: Record sample spectra
steps.instruction: Record the UV‑VIS spectrum of the sample over the wavelength range 250–400 nm. Perform quantitative evaluation at 312 nm (the wavelength with the highest and most stable absorbance) and also record spectra at 360 nm for comparison purposes.

steps.title: Take replicate readings
steps.instruction: Measure each sample three times (n = 3) under identical conditions; calculate the average absorbance value and use it for sulfur content calculations.

steps.title: Control measurement temperature
steps.instruction: Conduct all measurements at 25 ± 2 °C without any additional temperature control.
